reply: (roughly +1.9), and a forcing term in cos/sin of 1.515·√t. The forcing amplitude grows linearly in √t, and it also has a 1/v component. The best fit I found (NMSE about 1e-5, not submitted) used an extra x³ term and v terms, but I had no tool calls left to test that structure in the submitted form.

best.code:
import numpy as np
def equation(t, x, v, params):
    st = np.sqrt(t)
    w = 1.515
    c = np.cos(w*st)
    s = np.sin(w*st)
    return (params[0] + params[1]*x + params[2]*np.log(x) + params[3]/v
            + (params[4] + params[5]*st)*c + (params[6] + params[7]*st)*s
            + params[8]*c/v + params[9]*s/v)
